utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. All the accused are here. All the Defence teams are here, minus Mr. Bourgon. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. Ms. Frease is present in the courtroom. I suppose we can proceed. Mr. Zivanovic. And conclude. And after that, before we start with the next witness -- then after that, before we proceed, we need to address several issues and also give you some information. You would have noticed that we don't have Judge Stole with us this morning. But it will only be for a short while. He's got a personal problem to attend to and will be with us as soon as he can -- as he can, which is expected to be either during the duration of this first session, or the beginning of the second one. So good morning to you, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic will continue and finish his cross-examination within the next five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Frease, I would just like to clarify some things about the pages where the reports were collated that we talked about yesterday and that you explained that that was the result of exchange of information between different services that were intercepting conversations. What I'm interested in -- my question is, did you hear from anyone that reports were exchanged, not information, but that reports were exchanged between the military structures and those that are not military?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My memory is that the first time I heard that was during the course of an interview in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That reports were exchanged, not information, but reports. You do make a difference between those two things, of course.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, sorry. And my answer was imprecise as well. I remember during that interview first hearing that there was another agency working at the north site during an interview in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already told us that. Well, if you cannot answer this question, I will put the next one to you. Do you know whether a document drafted in the form that was given to you was given to any other organ of Bosnia and Herzegovina regardless of whether it was a military or a civilian organ?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And which document are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, all the time I'm talking about the binder of 550 pages or the documents that comprise that binder. We have already said that this is the printed material on perforated paper that was then cut and put together in the binder?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look at this binder and tell me -- you said that certain documents there do have dates. What I'm asking you is, if you recall or if you know whether there are documents in this binder where the dates are entered by hand, thus the copies of these documents would have the dates entered by hand in ink or felt-tip pen?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a vague recollection of there being a very small number, I mean, I'm thinking even like one, but you know, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to look at -- ask you to look at page 63 of this binder, please. We would just need to put the page on the ELMO. The page is -- [In English] Would you give the binder to the witness. She'll find it. [Interpretation] We have that page, yes. And if you can just scroll down a little bit, please. Thank you. You can see that the date there is entered by hand. My question is if you entered this date or somebody from the team, your team, or if the date was already written in the binder?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date would have already been written in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look at page 101 now, please. On the right-hand side of this document, at the top, you can see the date, and then there is one sentence is that states, "Description of the execution and expulsion of civilians."

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is something also that you or your team did not put in. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And we can say that the date and the sentence were written in the original, that this is not a photocopy of this document?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the document that we're looking at in the binder is a photocopy, and the ink, or the -- if I can just take -- and -- and to me this looks like a photocopy of what would have been on the original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Although you didn't see the original document at all, from what I understood. You only received photocopies, you did not receive the originals, did you?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is what we received, this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Excellent. And now, if you can just tell me, the photocopy, the date, the 16th of July, 1995, and the description of the execution and expulsion of civilians, this is something that was written in ink or felt-tip pen. It wasn't on the actual copy of the document, it was written on this copy of the original.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that from looking at this. To me this looks like -- like this -- what's written on here has been photocopied. For example, the last "a" is missing on here. I can't say for sure. It looks like it's been photocopied to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me if there is a difference between this text and the marking on the page, if you can look at page 101. You can see that the page is marked there at the top, it says "101."

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a difference between that page number, the ink used to indicate the page number, and this text that is written there below?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't look like it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's conclude this part. This clause, 16th of July, 1995, "description of the execution and expulsion of civilians," is something that was not added on later, that it was on the photocopy?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, it's the break-through of civilians, not the expulsion of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Frease, I'm going to put another question to you. We found out that there was a January, February mission in 1998. I'm sorry, I think that something was not entered into the transcript. The answer of the witness to my question on page 5, line 9 has not been entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, same comment -- same comment here. What happened, Mr. Zivanovic, was that you had barely finished your question when the interpreters butted in to make a correction. And because of that, I do not at least recall Ms. Frease answering your question. So perhaps we can go back to the question and she will answer it now. Do you still have it on your monitor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you answer that question, Ms. Frease, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to me it appears that this notation was not added later and that the second half of the question I find a little unclear, that it was on the photocopy. Yes, it's on the photocopy. I believe it was added at the time the photocopy was made. That's what it appears to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, at the time that the photocopy was made, somebody wrote this sentence in ink or felt-tip pen, is that what you're saying to say?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- try and follow as much as we can. We would like to see that page that the witness is being referred to. I'm sorry to interrupt you like this, Mr. Zivanovic, but I'm sure you understand. Still we are a little bit lost here. Question -- your answer was, "Yes, to me it appears that this notation was not added later and that the second half of the question I find a little unclear. That it was a photocopy -- that it was on the photocopy. Yes, it's on the photocopy. I believe it was added at the time the photocopy was made. That's what appears to me." Do you mean to say that it was already there when the photocopy was made, or that it was added at the time the photocopy was made? Because that's what we have in the transcript. And the two don't seem to merge harmoniously. Yes, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I find my answer also unclear. It seems to me that there was a notation on the page before a photocopy was made of that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's clear enough. Mr. Zivanovic, again my apologies. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to go back to the dispatch of these daily reports. Well, actually, before you actually talked about this January-February mission which preceded the March mission that we did not know about, incidentally. In light of the fact that it seems that at the time it was agreed that this selection of material, of intercept material is made and the binder is made, that is there in front of you, the binder of 550 pages. What I would like to ask you now, since as of March you are in charge of everything that has to do with intercept materials, what I would like to know is whether you were informed about that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with your statement that I was in charge of the intercept material from March. I wasn't on the March mission. I was there in April. It wasn't clear at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- at what point I would be put in charge of the intercept project or processing of the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In any case, you took over the duties, if not in March, then in April, from what I understood you as saying.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it really wasn't -- it wasn't that clear. There wasn't a date at which it was fixed that I took over the project. What I can tell you is that also I mean just -- to try -- I'm not sure whether this helps to clarify some of what we talked about yesterday with respect to the March 3rd document that Jean-Rene Ruez signed and then my notes saying that we received the material in March. My confusion about that comes from an "IIF" report, that would be in the transcript in IIF -- report that indicates, I believe, that someone else from the Office of the Prosecutor, that Peter Nicholson received this material on -- in April, at the end of April. I'm just trying to -- I'm trying to clarify --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that you are not answering my question. You're talking about a differently different topic, so I would like to ask you to answer my question, in view of the time I have at my disposal. I would like to ask you if you can to reply to my question. My question is, did you ever take over the duties of dealing exclusively with the intercepts? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the one other thing that I wanted to add that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just that in April we had already put together a small group of people to begin to process the intercepts. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, you've already told us about that, about the group of people in April. You've already told us during your examination-in-chief. The Prosecutor questioned you about that, and you gave an answer. So I don't know why you're repeating that. I assume, actually -- I know why you are repeating that, but if you can just reply to my question. At some point you took over custody, whether this was March, April or some other month. But anyway, they were entrusted to you and my question is, when you began to work on the intercepts, I assume that you were informed about what was happening after that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is, at one point you began the work on the intercepts, you began to be in charge of that work, and you were informed by your predecessors about what had happened or what had been done in that area to date. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, yesterday you took 22 minutes, and today you have already taken 20 minutes. Please bring your cross-examination to an end within the next five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, if you could tell me what an IIF report is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's an -- it's an internal document that is generated when people bring evidence back to the Court. It's a registration form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct if I say that the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina or the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did not want to give you the intercepts in the period from 1995 to March 1998 only because you did not want to agree for them to make the selection of the intercepts that would be handed over and that you agreed to this only in March of 1998?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'm going to move to my last topic. I would like to ask you to look at 5D189. That is page 3, paragraph 4. This is your report of the 24th of April. In the fourth paragraph there are two subtitles, one is "urgent messages" and the other one is "other message." Can you please read this and confirm for me the following: That this gentleman, I'm not going to mention his name, told you at the time that urgent messages were sent by telephone and then they were sent off by teleprinter. Other messages were sent only by teleprinter?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was just inquiring whether this page is being broadcast or not. I can confirm it is not being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that nothing was being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My view is always to make sure that is so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, you also received information that the messages were being sent by modem, that they were being encrypted first and so on and so forth, you know about that; right? You've heard about it, right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember knowing that specifically. I mean I remember learning about it later when, after I had left the court and these messages were provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is, did you ever check those allegedly encrypted messages that were sent off? Did you check the encryption, the decoding of those messages, all of those procedures of the messages that were sent in that form?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the two disks that we received while I was here, we were unable to open them. Our IT section was unable to open them and we were unable to open them. And after that, when I returned on this, during this period of time, I did not undertake a process of determining how the messages were coded and decoded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My last question is, is it possible that you did not do that because you knew that messages were not sent in that form at all, but exclusively by teleprinter?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. So I suppose that brings us to the end of the cross-examinations. Mr. Vanderpuye, you said yesterday you had a short re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you, good morning Your Honours, good morning counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, you've been asked a number of questions concerning this binder of 550 pages and I wonder if you could just tell us with respect to the intercepts that were compiled in relation to this particular case whether or not those 550 pages are included, first of all, within the binder collection? That is in physical form.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not included.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us to what extent, if any, those reports played in either the verifying of the intercepts or in the preparation of the materials or the intercepts that are offered by the Prosecution in this case?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: They provided background, and provided us an ability to be able to find the cleaner electronic copies that we are using in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity at any point to compare transcriptions as they appeared in the hard copies of the 550 page binder against transcriptions as they appeared as a result of printing out the electronic versions of those intercepts?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you find that there existed textual differences with respect to the conversations that were transcribed between the two?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were also asked some questions by my colleague --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were none, let me be --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were also asked some questions by my colleague about a certain --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness please make pauses between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, you've both heard what the interpreter enjoins you to do. Please comply. It creates big problems for the interpreters, so I encourage you to be as cooperative as you can. Thank you. --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I apologise to the court. I'm just trying to be as brief as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were asked some questions by my colleague about a conversation that occurred on April 20th, I believe it was, between Mr. Popovic and Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in particular you were asked about the transcription of tape recording of that conversation and whether or not the presence or absence of certain words changed the meaning or reliability of the content, as you determined it? Do you recall being asked questions to that effect?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can I ask you, did you review any documentation or was any documentation brought to your attention with respect to the veracity as to the content of that communication?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I have please P02467 displayed in e-court, please. I just want to inquire whether or not this is being broadcast. I would assume not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I assume not as well, but I better check.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Not broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, do you recognise what's displayed in e-court now?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what that is, for the record?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an order that was issued by the Drina Corps command with a confidential number at the top dated the 20th of April. It's directed to the command of the Zvornik Brigade. And it references a document, an order that had been issued to the Drina Corps command by the Main Staff of the VRS with respect to the deployment of two volunteers, Polish volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And in your view, is this corroborative of the intercept communication of the 20th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I have also another document displayed in e-court, please. That is P02469. Do we have a linkage problem? We do. Okay. I can hand the witness a document on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if you could kindly do that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, Ms. Frease, do you recognise this document? Could you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document that is a list of Polish volunteers, the title of it says a list, it's in B/C/S. Maybe I should just read it out loud and the interpreters can translate it. [Interpretation] "List of fighters killed of the Zvornik Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now could I just refer your attention, if I could -- you will have to turn some pages to get to it, but to page number 17.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you give me an ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yeah, the ERN number is 0082-4652. And if I could at the same time have P02467 displayed again on e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 3 again?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: P02467 is one page. This isn't being broadcast, right? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, if I could just refer your attention to the name that is preceded by the number 2 on that page. Do you see that name? Just don't read it out, but do you see it?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me refer your attention to the document you have in front of you on the ELMO and can I refer your attention to number 450 on that page? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does the name that appears on 450 on ERN 0082-4652, does that correspond to the number 2 on the document that's displayed in e-court?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it appears to. There are some misspellings in the name, in the first and last name, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that corroborative of the intercept that's dated 20th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just move on to another area, if I could.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You indicated in response to some questions put to you by my colleague, Mr. Ostojic, you were put some questions about an intercept involving Mr. Beara, a series of three intercepts, one at 9.55, one at 9.57 and one at 10.00 a.m. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if the course of that testimony you indicated that there was an intercept that was corroborative of that 15 July intercept which was on the 13th of July at 19.19; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 1147A, please, displayed in e-court. I think the B/C/S version of it is B. All right. Do you see what's displayed in e-court now?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this the intercept to which you had previously referred?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, first of all, how you assessed this particular intercept as corroborative of the intercept referred to by my colleague, Mr. Ostojic, during his questioning of you involving Mr. Beara on the morning of the 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several points. The content of this information -- of this intercept, from the 13th of July at 19.19 references individuals and locations that I'm aware of that -- that confirm the information that Mr. Beara referred to in the conversations from 9.55, 9.57 and 10.00 on the -- on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. In particular, can you tell us what it is that Mr. Beara refers to in the intercept on the 15th that has bearing on this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my memory, he talks about the fact that he needs 15 to 30 of Indzic's guys. He first starts off saying that Furtula, who is the commander of the Visegrad Brigade wasn't following the commanders orders and that he needed 15 to 30 of Indzic's guys.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I just stop you for a second. Can you tell us, if you know, what the relationship between Indzic is to Furtula?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the three intercepts from the 13th -- from the 15th of July, I think it's the one at 9.57, could be the one at 10.00 too, I'm not sure, but it says that Boban Indzic is Fortula's deputy. So in that conversation from the 15th of July, Colonel Beara goes on to say that if the commander's orders had been carried out and if things had been done on the 13th, then he wouldn't still be asking for the -- I don't remember the exact word that he used, but for -- for what he was asking for on the 15th, which were Indzic's guys, Boban Indzic's guys.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does this give -- this particular intercept give an indication as to what happened to those guys, as you put it, on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, their bus broke down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I just -- just a moment. Could we have 65 ter 1179H and I, please, on the e-court. All right. Do you recognise what's displayed in e-court now?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm going to refer you to the page on the left, third line up or so from the bottom. Do you see -- well, not anymore. Was the third line up from the bottom. I think it is still now the third line up from the bottom. Could you take a look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you just tell us how that relates to the intercept that you've described on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- it says, "Indzic, Indzic, Lukic's deputy."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Is there a specific reference to 30 men?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 15 to 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could just go down a little bit, please. Now, I just want to refer you to what appears to be the eighth line up from the bottom. Now, you had indicated previously that there was some portion of the conversation which Mr. Beara purportedly was essentially saying that -- essentially saying that he hadn't received the 30 men, the 15 to 30 men, is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, that that's what he needed, 15 to 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you can identify that on this intercept? You have to answer for the record. If you can.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us where it is in the intercept and what it says?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's halfway through on that first page where it says, "Look, I need 15 to 30 men with Boban Indzic."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see a reference lower down in the intercept specifically where Mr. Beara purportedly says, "I don't have any"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "And that's why I'm asking for the third day."

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to that particular statement, do you -- tell me what you understand that to mean, what he doesn't have?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he doesn't have the 15 to 30 men that he needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The reference to the third day is the 15th?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does that relate to the prior intercept on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How so?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were supposed to be men from Indzic's group, Boban Indzic's group who were supposed to arrive and they didn't, they couldn't, because their vehicle broke down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had indicated previously that there was a reference to Boban Indzic, and Indzic was Furtula's deputy. You see here on this intercept, there is a reference to Indzic being Lukic's deputy?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, if you know, who Lukic was or is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that it refers to Milan Lukic, who was from Visegrad. But that's as much as I can -- as much as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me refer you to a -- well, just a moment. 1179A and B. A is the English version, please. In e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please tell me the time of the intercept? Because we have two documents in e-court under the same 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think it's 10.00. This is 9.57 still, what's in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have the hard copy? We will move faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You know what, I think I can move to a different area while we try locate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were asked a number of questions by my learned colleague, Mr. Ostojic, about a certain reference allegedly made on the 15th of July, 1995, concerning some certain parcels.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you were asked particularly whether or not you had made inquiry of intercept operators about the meaning of the particular term. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to the meaning of that particular term, did you determine, through reference to other materials, what was meant by that term?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one reference in particular comes to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I refer to the index?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Which index are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The index to the intercepted conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No problem with us, but does any of the Defence teams have any problems? No. Okay. Go ahead, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a conversation on the 2nd of August at 1240 involving Krstic and Popovic in which -- I'll -- may I just read the summary? It says, "It's Popovic. Go ahead boss. Get over to Bajina Basta. You know what you have to do. He has sent -- he has set out towards me -- towards me." That's a question. "He's on his way. He went up there because he had some parcels to check what they know."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If I could have 65 ter 1164A and B, please, on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, can we get the 65 ter number of the intercept Ms. Frease just read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: August 2nd.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have it. 1392.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think the English version on the left is not corresponding to the B/C/S version on the right. The B/C/S version is several pages and that's the beginning of it on the right, but the English version doesn't seem to correspond to it. Is there a following page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can someone help us in this? I don't think it corresponds too, but I want someone to assure us of that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There are two exhibits under 1164B.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Two exhibits under 1164B. Well, all right. I'm referring to the one specifically on 14th July at 2102. In the meantime, I have a hard copy I can provide to the witness. Maybe we can proceed with the ELMO. All right. I think we have it. Thank you. Could I just go to the second page of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There's only one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think on page 21, line 21, he's looking for the 14th and I think this document, from other witnesses, was established another date, and I thought Ms. Frease already testified that it was -- she thought the 15th. I'm not sure if counsel is referring to this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm actually referring to the 14th. Insofar as it relates to the definition of "parcel."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wanted to make sure Mr. Ostojic is okay with that. So let's try and go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Frease, if I could refer you to -- all right. Do you see where it says, "Number 55" in the middle of the page, on the left, in the English version?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could refer you to just a couple of lines below that, do you see a reference to "parcels" in that line?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you just read that into the record?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's J speaking. He says, "There are big problems. Well, with the people. I mean, with the parcel."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does that in any -- in your evaluation of what the term "parcel" meant, did that play any role in determining what the meaning was?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And based upon that, is that consistent with your understanding of what the term "parcel" means?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I refer you to an intercept on August 1st at 2245 hours. The 65 ter number on that one is 1380A and B. If I could, I'm just going to refer you to -- if you can see, it appears to be a full paragraph in the English version that's attributed allegedly to Mr. Beara. Could you read that into the record and tell us what your assessment in terms of what the definition of "parcels" is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's B who is defined as Ljubisa Beara, "From Caura, we were there. Now we have just returned. Zoka Cavcic was also with us. So far there are about 300 parcels. They, whoever captures a parcel hands it over to the cops and now they are keeping that. I've talked to the chief of the SUP (secretariat of the interior) from Uzice. He says, 'I can't do anything for you now but we'll be in touch. But the chiefs have to make a decision as to what they want to do.' So we should now tell our chief and the supreme chief. They -- this is the information confirmed by my people. There are up to 1.000 parcels in the place which is like ours. It's all crammed in over there. They said there was big trouble over there. Some commotion and so on. But he says that you can't do anything because those are valleys, caves and nothing can be done there. Small parcels go first and the big ones are left for the end. And they will probably all go in the same direction."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, do you see, following that line, a further statement attributed to Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And that statement reads, "We can't do that. Morina was here and she brought some people from the ICRC and the UNHCR and they filmed a pile of parcels, the motherfuckers, and they'll show that on TV." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Given what you see on this page, is that something that you considered in determining how to attribute a meaning to the word "parcels"?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is it consistent with your understanding that it meant people?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Bear with me for one moment. Now, you were also asked some questions concerning extension 155?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I don't recall exactly who asked the question, although I think it might have been my colleague, Mr. Beara -- I mean Mr. Ostojic, excuse me, Mr. Ostojic. And I believe you were asked some specific questions about that and you indicated, or it was suggested to you that that extension corresponded to Tolimir, and you responded that that was not the information that you had. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And could you tell us what information it is that you had concerning that particular extension?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that that was General Manojlo Milovanovic's extension, but he was away for a period of several months, during this period of time, and that in his absence General Miletic was using extension 155.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter 2438A and B, please, displayed in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like the Prosecutor to specify with the witness where it is that she gets this information, how does she come to those conclusions and I would also like for some additional time for a -- additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very pertinent remark, Madam Fauveau. Could you please address that, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Address where the witness got the information? I think that's exactly the question I put to her. Or maybe not. I asked her what information she had, so I guess I'll follow and ask -- well, what's the source of that information, if that will satisfy my colleague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's exactly what your colleague wants to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should answer that question before we continue. In an investigation one accumulates a lot of knowledge, and with respect to General Milovanovic's absence, I don't remember -- I can't put a specific document to that. But an intercept from the 28th of October references extension 155, and various inquiries have been made, and we've looked through the intercepts for references to 155, and I believe that there are also other witnesses who have -- who have knowledge about the -- that extension and who was working on that extension at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. May I refer, please, to 65 ter 2438. I think it's A and B.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this intercept, Ms. Frease?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this the intercept to which you just made reference?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us how you derive from this particular intercept -- how you can attribute that extension to either Milovanovic or Miletic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could just take a minute to read through the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While the witness is examining this document, could I please have the exact reference of this intercept?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you mean the 65 ter number? I believe I said it was 65 ter 2438A and B.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but was this document on the 65 ter list? Because this number was not on the 65 ter list. Not on the initial list anyway. It must be an added exhibit, and I would like to know if the Prosecutor requested the authorisation to add this document on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I can answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe that this particular intercept was added -- was the result of the January 10th decision of the Court permitting the addition of nine intercepts. I think in other motion we called them 10, because two of them were precisely from the same date. The Court had ruled on it. In fact, I think perhaps as recently as last week or a week and a half ago when the Court made its decision on whether or not to add an intercept operator, there was a specific reference to the decision talking about the relevance of an intercept that was dated January the 19th in that same motion this intercept was a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I believe you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Have you had an opportunity to review the -- the intercept, Ms. Frease?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us how this relates to General Miletic or Milovanovic, as you've indicated?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: About one-third of the way down on the conversation -- in the conversation, P, who I guess is Panorama says, "Just a moment, General, nobody is answering at that extension." Then they say then, "Give me 155 right away." And then M says, "Milovanovic." X says, "Hey Mane, tell me, I needed Miletic or one of those who give permits." And then it goes on, "Did you promise anything to Balas."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did that leave you with the impression that the person that asked for the extension was trying to reach General Miletic at that extension?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that the reason why you drew the conclusion, if you did, that that extension was associated with General Miletic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for that reason. But there's also other -- other knowledge which I can't pinpoint right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Is it fair to say that this was part of the reason that you drew that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, and did you rely on other information provided to you by investigators, military analysts and so on?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to refer you back, if I could, this hopefully will take only a minute. I had referred you previously to an intercept on August the 1st where you had read out a long paragraph. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And at the beginning of the paragraph there was a reference to Caura?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us where that is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- it's the Visegrad Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And then there's a further reference to, "We were there and we've just returned."

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know what the -- what's being spoken about here? I would like to -- if it's possible, to put those conversations back up on the screen, that would be helpful to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 1380A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that -- well, what they're referring to is what Colonel Beara is referring to as having returned from Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us where that is?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's across the river, it's in Serbia. It across the Drina River in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that related to the conversation that you indicated that occurred, I think, on August the 2nd?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there -- conversations on the -- from the 1st to the 3rd, I think that relate to this issue. Is there one more thing that I could say just about this Zoka Cavcic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that is a -- a typographical -- well, not -- maybe not a typographical error, but that the intercept operator didn't hear the name correctly. Because I believe it should be Zoka, Zoka is a nickname for Zoran, first name Zoran, and there's -- the last name, instead of Cavcic, I believe, should be Carkic. They sound very similar. And Zoran Carkic was the security person at the Visegrad Brigade. At Caura -- Caura was the nickname for the Visegrad Brigade, so that ties it, it's very consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you for that. And did you consider that, by the way, in assessing the reliability of the content of this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is it consistent with your understanding, historical and otherwise, as concerns the events in and around the 1st of August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you have any indication in relation to the parcels that are being spoken about in this intercept, where they might have originated from and where they were located?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That they had mostly originated from Zepa, and that they were at that point located in Serbia in Bajina Basta, having swam or somehow made it across the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And based upon your review of the intercepts is concerned, that particular matter, did you have an opportunity to review an intercept in which General Krstic was a participant in and around August 2nd of 1995?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recall just basically the substance of that intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was an intercept that had been picked up by both the northern and the southern site for which we played -- we also had the audio recordings and played those in court. It's a conversation between General Krstic and Major Obrenovic from the Zvornik Brigade, the deputy. The time in which they're talking about having encircled or trapped -- trapped people on minefields and General Krstic says, "Well, kill them all, goddamn it, kill them all."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry, you were asked some questions -- hang on one second. Bear with me one moment. You were asked some questions about the name Ljubo?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I think it was put to you specifically that there was a person whose name appears in the intercept by the name of Ljubo Bojanovic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I think my colleague had essentially asked you if there was -- you had some ability to distinguish between the name Ljubo as a full name, first name, and as a nickname, whether or not you were able to identify or distinguish essentially between Bojanovic and Beara, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I ask you, are you able to do that, or were you able to do that in looking at these intercepts?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And how were you able to do that, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember I think there are three conversations on the 23rd of July. One of them references a Major Bojanovic, and I think the one or two others might just reference Ljubo, and it was -- it also happens that on that date he was the duty officer at the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to your ability to distinguish between the two, did you do that as a result of how the name appeared in the -- in the intercept itself or did you do that as a result of analysing the context in which the name was used?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the context in which the name was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you remember a specific context in which the name was used?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I refer to the index?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one of them his name comes up just as Bojanovic, Major Bojanovic, and not as Ljubo at all. And that's on the 23rd of July at 6.40 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Could I have, please, 65 ter 1307A and B displayed in e-court, please. All right. Do you see what's displayed in e-court now, Ms. Frease?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this the intercept that you had previously -- you have just spoken about?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us how, in this case -- well, tell us how in this case you were able to determine according to this intercept, who B is attributed to? Do you see the letter B?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, based on your view of this intercept, who that relates to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in this particular intercept, I think you had indicated that as a result of context you could determine that it was Major Bojanovic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, because he was the duty officer. And he was -- this conversation is between General Krstic and Major Bojanovic. It starts off with Major -- sorry, General Krstic saying, Is everything all right? And Major Bojanovic giving a report essentially of what had happened that previous night, that there were some attacks, mainly without casualties, that he says here that six Turks were captured. And then it goes on to give an update of what's happening, that the detention facility is full, there are more than 30 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Are there any other intercepts that come to mind with respect to the identification or distinction that you can draw between the name Ljubo as it's applied to Bojanovic or as it's applied to Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's this one at 8.05 also on the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what your recollection is of that intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to put it, I think, in a little bit of context. It's a -- the conversation previous to that is one at 8.00 in the morning between Vinko and an unknown participant in which in my -- in the summary it says, Vinko says, We're still catching Turks. I have some prisoners, I have some wounded. I don't know what to do with them, where to send them. Did anyone talk about an exchange for those guys from Lisaca, that letter arrived stating the wounded should be sent to Zvornik hospital however there is a problem with that and I would ask you for a solution today. And then in the next conversation this same unknown participant, who is indicated in both of these conversations by a question mark, says that this unknown participant says in a previous conversation he called and asked for Vinko again but Ljubo answered. And I believe that's Ljubo Bojanovic again because he was the duty officer at Zvornik Brigade headquarters that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. I'm sorry to interrupt you like that. Yes, General Miletic. THE ACCUSED MILETIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, what is she talking about? Perhaps we can have it put on the screen. And on the screen at the moment we can see a previous transcript of an intercept. We would just like to be able to follow and see on the screen what the witness is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's a fair comment, General Miletic. Ms. Frease --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have the 65 ter numbers. I just wanted the witness to give the background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But General Miletic is perfectly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She is reading in English. Perhaps it is being translated of course. But the question is not just receiving an interpretation, it's also seeing the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No problem. I notice the time. And I won't put it up in the e-court. I just suspect it will take probably longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we will have the break here, and after the break, we will take this matter up again. And be prepared, please, to have it on e-court. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Judge Stole is not yet back from his appointment. As soon as he arrives he will come into -- in here and join us. So for the time being, and until then, we will continue sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis, all right. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye, Ms. Frease and also do we have -- can we put on e-court the document that Ms. Frease was reading from or to which she was being referred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can we just make one little correction to the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Frease.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At 34/7 at 10.30.21 there was a "but Ljubo", I think, but it should have been -- and I think -- sorry, I think it says "for Ljubo" and it should say "but Ljubo" answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So instead of "asked for Vinko again for Ljubo answered," it should be "asked for Vinko again but Ljubo answered."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we were last in the process of displaying the intercepts that Ms. Frease had referred to, the first of which is the 8.00 intercept on the 23rd of July. The 65 ter number for that one is 1309. Okay. I think we have that in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you take a look at that, Ms. Frease?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this the intercept that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what about this intercept is indicative of the following one, the 8.05 intercept that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the following conversation refers to the previous conversation between the same two unknown participants, but -- and I don't have the text of the 8.05 conversation. I'm sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We'll put that up in a minute.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, of course. But this one indicates that they -- here, V, Vinko Pandurevic is saying, "Well, we're still catching Turks. I have some prisoners. I have some wounded. I don't know what to do with them, where to send them."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could please have 65 ter 13 -- 1310. 1310, I think that's probably A and B as well, displayed in e-court. Okay. Do you see what's displayed in e-court now?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this the conversation to which you'd previously referred?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And having evaluated this particular intercept, it's your position that the Ljubo that's referred to in this intercept is not Ljubisa Beara?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is Ljubo Bojanovic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And why -- is that because of the context of the intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were asked several questions concerning changes, modifications or alterations that were made particular to an intercept involving Mr. Beara. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you circled and marked on a document indicating certain changes or modifications that you found on the respective intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, in evaluating the collection of intercepts, looking at the notebooks, did you come across changes of that nature, cross-outs, things of that nature, that were done in a manner that was inconsistent with the process by which the interceptors described these transcriptions took place?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And that concludes my re-direct examination. Thank you, Ms. Frease. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to request leave to ask a few additional questions an P2438 that was not at all foreseen to be used with this witness and that refers directly to my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's your position on that, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection, but I would like to examine the witness about the documents used by the Prosecutor in redirect. It's practically only one document, and that's 2469.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is your position on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: To the extent that Mr. Zivanovic is asking for leave to re-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The document was presented to the witness, I don't see that it's outside the scope of redirect examination, so I think it's appropriate. I would defer to the Court's discretion with respect to the scope that would be permitted, but I think it's -- it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Madam Fauveau first and then we'll come to you, Mr. Zivanovic, and Mr. Ostojic. I think -- yes. Go ahead, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think I am also asking for leave to conduct a recross of this witness based on some of the questions that were raised during --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Which areas?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which areas do you want to recross the witness about?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Utilisation of an intercept that was not testified to during her direct examination; namely, the October 23rd, 1995 intercept. Also, utilisation and identification of Ljubo Bojanovic on 65 ter 1307. Also what she claims to be testimony of who this Lukic is and obviously on page 19, line 17, she used the word "I assume." I'm going to ask her if that is just pure speculation on her part. Specifically, I'll also ask her on 65 ter 1147A which she now claims, although did not during her direct examination, that that was corroborative evidence of any other intercepts, specifically, the intercept dated the 15th of July, 1995. And then also with respect to her identification of Ljubo, whether she's identified, based upon her purported knowledge of B/C/S, whether there was a dialect difference in any of Ljubo Bojanovic's intercepts, if she could detect what his dialect was from and if it was consistent with the other ones she claims now were Mr. Beara's. Also, I was going to ask her a question with respect to this extension 155, that they claim is now somebody else. And my question to that point, regardless of who is extension 155. Then there it clearly indicates that the purported participant, Mr. Beara, did not know whether it was General Milovanovic or anyone at that extension. And then I wanted to know what her information is as to what role Mr. Milovanovic had in the Main Staff or any position she thinks he held at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose none of you requires a lecture from us on the limits to recross. Could I have a printout of this part of Mr. Ostojic's intervention, please. Let's start with you, Madam Fauveau, if you restrict yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Fauveau and all the others, as you know that -- yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to my learned friend Mr. Ostojic's submission concerning the scope of the proposed recross-examination, I do object to that one. And the reason why I object to it is I think there are a couple of things that maybe I should bring to the Court's attention. I'm sure that you've probably already considered that. But first of all, with respect to the October 28th intercept, it's reflected 23rd in the transcript, I think he means the 28th. Now with respect to that intercept, that relates specifically to the identification of the extension 155 that Mr. Ostojic rather put to the witness, not my colleague, Madam Fauveau. So it is relevant to the extent that perhaps Madam Fauveau wants to question the witness or recross-examine the witness on -- as concerns what we have put forward is the extension of her client. But is not with respect to Mr. Ostojic in terms of his recross-examination of the witness. And the reason for it is directly responsive to an issue that was broached by Mr. Ostojic. And he had the opportunity obviously on cross-examination to explore that issue. It's not a surprise intercept; it's an intercept that actually was the subject of -- of considerable motion practice, and of which he was aware. And to the extent that that issue was broached on cross-examination, he had that opportunity at that point to confront the witness with the intercept to the extent that he differs with her interpretation of it as she has put forward today. With respect to 65 ter number 1148, I refer to 65 ter number 1147 on redirect examination. I think maybe that is what Mr. Ostojic is referring to. In any event, that is the 13th of July 19.19 intercept which was also raised in response direct response to a question that was put to the witness by Mr. Ostojic in his cross-examination in the first instance. Specifically asked her -- he specifically asked her, and if you bear with me for one moment, I think I can get the precise question. He specifically asked her about corroboration with respect to the -- to the July 15th intercept and in response to that questioning the witness indicated that she had referred to an -- to an intercept on the 13th of July, 19.19 which was directly corroborative of the July 15th intercept. That was on cross-examination. It wasn't elicited on direct and is directly responsive, obviously, to the issue that arose during cross-examination because Mr. Ostojic elicited that. If there was a question as to what her interpretation was of that intercept or what it contained, or the conclusions she draw from -- drew from it or how it was corroborative of the 15th of July intercept involving his client, he had every opportunity on cross-examination to do that. There was no objection, there was no limitation to the scope of the cross-examination as concerns that particular issue. With respect to the extension 155 as concerns the questioning by Mr. Ostojic, he also put forward that it was information or the position of the Defence that that extension corresponded to Tolimir and the witness responded that's not what her information was. And that is I think the grounds upon which -- that was opened on re-direct examination. To the extent that she had represented that her information was different to know what her information was. And I think there was some question about what was the basis of the information, which I think we -- was explained on re-direct examination through the examination of these various intercepts that indicate at least to the witness to whom that particular extension is ascribed. So I don't think that Mr. Ostojic, my colleague, has set forth any grounds upon which to permit re-cross-examination to the extent that he actually elicited most of the information, it was -- that was the subject of the re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Madam Fauveau, go ahead. We'll come to each one of you. In your case there is no objection on the part of the Prosecution, and therefore we grant you the exceptional -- exceptional possibility to re-cross-examine the witness. For the record I notice that Mr. Bourgon is in the courtroom. Yes, Madam Fauveau. How long do you expect to be?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe 20 minutes, 15 to 20, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are limiting your cross-examination to that particular intercept document that you mentioned earlier, Madam Fauveau, and to nothing else, so we're giving you five minutes to do that, please. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness Exhibit P2438.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it true that General Milovanovic first requested to speak to a colonel?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And that colonel could have been one of the subordinates of General Miletic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would just be speculation. It's unclear who this colonel is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Very well. And then he asked to speak to a certain Dubovina?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And then the third thing, or the third person or the third extension was number 155?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when the person on extension 155 answered General Milovanovic, that person was not General Miletic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And General Milovanovic said, "I was looking for Miletic." He didn't say "I am looking for Miletic". Is that true?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I think there is a mistake in the transcript. General Miletic did not say "I am looking for Miletic," he said in the past, "I was looking for Miletic?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is another mistake in the transcript, line 11. It's not General Miletic who said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Indeed, it was General Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So your answer -- your question, Madam Fauveau, was General Milovanovic said "I was looking for Miletic", he didn't say I was -- "I am looking for Miletic." Is that correct? Would you agree to that Ms. Frease?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I see the B/C/S version, the next page of the -- of the B/C/S version? But yes, in English it says "I needed Miletic or one of those who gives permits. Who give permits, it says, but who gives permits. Hmm...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You speak B/C/S. Is it true that the first sentence is also in the past tense, that the B/C/S version also says, "I was looking for Miletic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do the words [B/C/S spoken], as they appear in the transcript, if I am reading them well, mean? Is that in the present tense or in the past tense or in the past perfect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say in the B/C/S it should be [B/C/S spoken] which would be past tense. But yes, this is -- this is -- yes, this should be past tense. It says -- it's a slightly shortened version for what I know of the past tense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would it not be logical, if General Miletic was on extension 155, that General Miletic [sic] would have said I need Miletic, please give me Miletic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it's a question that should be asked. It can become a submission. Are you in a position to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not -- no, not really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's being put to you that if General Miletic was on -- available on 155, or would have been available on 155, Milovanovic would have said I need to speak to Miletic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe he just wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
